Task: How to Wrap a Box With a Square End
The action list you can take: ['Cut four pieces of ribbon for the width of the box.
', 'Wrap lengthwise - Bring the paper so that it wraps around the box lengthwise, leaving an equal amount of paper at each end.
', 'Fold the end - At one end of the box, fold the paper down.', 'Measure the ends - Make sure there is slightly more than half the depth of the box at each end.', 'Repeat - Repeat this at the other end of the box, folding the paper down, the sides and the bottom up.', 'Fold in 2 opposing corners so they meet point-to-point in the center of your square.
', 'Cut four pieces of ribbon for the length of the box.
', 'Stitch the box together using a ¼-inch (0.64-centimeter) seam allowance.
', 'Finished.', 'Next, securely tape down the box and add tape for additional support to the corners of the box to make it even more secure.
', 'Wrap lengthwise - Bring the paper so that it wraps around the box lengthwise, leaving an equal amount of paper at each end.', 'Measure the paper - Ensure that you have secured anything fragile inside your box and turn the box upside down.', 'For bottom of box, cut the square 1/4 " smaller than the top.
', 'Glue your piece of brown construction paper designed with puffy paint (must wait for puffy paint to DRY COMPLETELY) on the top of the box.
', 'Wrap the ribbons around the box and secure them with double-sided tape.
', 'Glue your cut construction paper onto one side of the box.
']

1. Cut four pieces of ribbon for the width of the box.
2. Wrap lengthwise - Bring the paper so that it wraps around the box lengthwise, leaving an equal amount of paper at each end.
3. Measure the ends - Make sure there is slightly more than half the depth of the box at each end.
4. Fold the end - At one end of the box, fold the paper down.
5. Repeat - Repeat this at the other end of the box, folding the paper down, the sides and the bottom up.
6. Fold in 2 opposing corners so they meet point-to-point in the center of your square.
7. Cut four pieces of ribbon for the length of the box.
8. Stitch the box together using a ¼-inch (0.64-centimeter) seam allowance.
9. Finished.
10. Next, securely tape down the box and add tape for additional support to the corners of the box to make it even more secure.
11. Measure the paper - Ensure that you have secured anything fragile inside your box and turn the box upside down.
12. For bottom of box, cut the square 1/4 " smaller than the top.
13. Glue your piece of brown construction paper designed with puffy paint (must wait for puffy paint to DRY COMPLETELY) on the top of the box.
14. Glue your cut construction paper onto one side of the box.
15. Wrap the ribbons around the box and secure them with double-sided tape.

5. Slide the rags or cardboard into the shirt to protect the back from being bleached.
6. Pour bleach into a glass container or measuring cup.

8. Blot the shirt all around the design.

10. Wait for the bleach to take effect.
11. Remove the rags or cardboard and rinse the shirt in cold water.
12. Run the clothes under cold water to deactivate the bleach.
13. Put the bleached clothing in the washer and clean using soap powder.
14. Use a bleach-free clothing detergent.
15. Dry the shirt accordingly.
16. Place your dyed shirt in a sealable plastic bag or garbage bag for 24 hours.
